Subject: Post-call recap: PayBridge auth choices + next steps for SDK & key management

Thanks again for the time this morning — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key takeaways from today's discovery:
- PayBridge prefers server-to-server authentication for inference workloads (low-latency backend calls).
- Security requirement: audit logs of token/key usage + enforced rotation cadence (TBD, you mentioned ~90 days).
- Important to scope expected QPS and burst patterns before we size caching/connection pooling.

Recommended items we promised to follow up with: 
1) Short architecture sketch for the flow you asked about (service account JWT -> Redwood API -> per-request routing). Attached: arch-draft.drawio.png.
2) A matrix of auth options, pros/cons and implementation effort (attached: auth-options-table.xlsx).
3) SDK snippets for Node/Python showing automatic key refresh and short-lived token exchange (see message from Marissa below).

Questions for you to confirm before the tech deep-dive: 
- Do you want Redwood-managed API keys for application-level traffic, or do you prefer service accounts + signed JWTs that you control in your KMS?
- Any compliance constraints around bringing keys into a hosted flow (e.g., keys must remain in your HSM)?

Proposed next steps (pick what works):
- Engineer-to-engineer PoC call (30m) to walk through JWT flow + SDK integration — we have availability Wed 2/25 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 2/26 afternoon.
- If you confirm service account approach, we can prepare a 1–2 day PoC to exchange a short-lived token and run a few inference calls.

Attachments: rwd-paybridge-auth-proposal.pdf, arch-draft.drawio.png, auth-options-table.xlsx

Thanks — I’ve looped Marissa and Neha for technical follow-up and scheduling.

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers from our side: 

- We are leaning toward service accounts + signed JWTs issued from our KMS (we want to avoid long-lived static API keys).
- Rotation: security policy is 90 days for any credential; short-lived tokens (<= 1 hour) are preferred for runtime.
- We need proof that Redwood supports KMS-backed signing or a flow that keeps private keys in our HSM. Can Redwood do token exchange where we sign JWTs internally and Redwood validates without ingesting private key material?
- Audit logs: we need per-token/per-request logs retained for at least 12 months (access logs + token id mapping).

Also, please include the cost delta (rough order of magnitude) between using Redwood Hosted with service-account flow vs. Dedicated pool for our projected QPS (~30 rps sustained, 200 rps burst for 30s).

Let's do the engineer PoC. Wed 2/25 10:00 PT works for Mark (security) and me. Can Marissa/Neha and a solutions engineer join?

Alex — good questions. Technical clarifications below (engineer-to-engineer level).

Summary of viable auth options (see attached matrix for more detail):
1) API keys (simple) — Redwood-hosted API keys, long-lived unless you rotate; easiest to prototype but not recommended for strict HSM requirements.
2) Service accounts + JWT signed by customer (recommended) — you keep private keys in your KMS/HSM, sign a short-lived JWT (<= 1h) that we validate with your public key. SDK can handle caching of the JWT and re-sign-negotiation on expiry. Supports audit logs and token-id mapping.
3) OAuth2 client credentials (server-to-server) — similar to JWT flow but involves token endpoint; good if you want an issuer-managed lifecycle.

Implementation notes / Redwood capabilities: 
- Support for JWK set / public key rotation: Redwood accepts a jwks_uri or published public keys and will validate incoming JWTs; we do NOT require the private key material.
- Short-lived token flow: recommended pattern is customer signs a JWT with kid that maps to a key in your jwks_uri; Redwood validates and issues a session id for request-level mapping.
- SDKs (Node/Python) include helper modules to fetch/refresh signed tokens and attach them to inference calls. Example pseudo-code (Node):
  const {JWTClient} = require('@redwood/sdk');
  const client = new JWTClient({jwksUri: 'https://keys.paybridge.com/.well-known/jwks.json', signFn: yourSignFn});
  const token = await client.getSignedToken();
  const resp = await client.infer({model: 'redwood-rlhf-large', input: '...'});

- Audit logs: we can surface token kid, session id, request id, model, latency, and response code to your SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch/BigQuery export. Retention and export format configurable (12 months retention supported).
- HSM note: if your policy forbids sending any private key material into hosted systems, the JWT-signed-by-you approach meets that requirement. We validate public keys only.

Attachments: auth-options-table.xlsx (detailed matrix). Also shared a draft proposal PDF and architecture sketch in the Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b-paybridge-auth

I can take lead on the PoC setup. For the calendar invite, who should be invited from PayBridge besides Alex and Mark from security?
